PullRequest.Title: Agents - refactor repository pickers so that all actions are in one toolbar

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The event source, synchronous refresh, microtask-coalesced structural menu notification, and toolbar disposal/recreation path are all directly traced in repository code. The exact frame cost varies by the number of visible sessions and provider-defined properties, so severity is medium, but the repeated rendering mechanism is certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Repository-toolbar action objects, picker instances, event listeners, and DOM nodes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each provider config pulse causes one coalesced structural menu update; every live NewSessionRepositoryConfig toolbar then disposes and recreates all P repository picker items, so work grows as O(V×P) for V visible session composers and P renderable config properties. A normal draft selection produces at least an optimistic pulse and a later resolution pulse.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unnecessary main-thread DOM/allocation work and GC pressure during branch/worktree interactions, increasing interaction latency and risking visible jank as visible sessions and schema properties grow.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The repository menu contained one statically registered action. Provider config pulses re-rendered the existing composite picker in place, without mutating MenuRegistry or forcing MenuWorkbenchToolBar.setActions to dispose and recreate the entire toolbar.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new provider-wide listener calls _refreshRepositoryMenuItems for every onDidChangeSessionConfig event, regardless of which session changed or whether the renderable schema changed; that method clears and re-appends menu items, publishing a structural menu change consumed by every toolbar.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT-side line 1545 registers `provider.onDidChangeSessionConfig(() => this._refreshRepositoryMenuItems(actionViewItemService))`; before this PR there was no provider-config listener that mutated the repository MenuRegistry.
Findings.Title: Avoid structurally rebuilding every repository toolbar on value changes
Findings.Impact: Selecting a branch or isolation option fires onDidChangeSessionConfig synchronously before the existing asynchronous config resolution and again when resolution completes. Both value-only events now rebuild each visible repository toolbar, recreating all per-property controls even though the set/order/titles of actions usually did not change.
Findings.Evidence: The added listener at line 1545 ignores the event's sessionId and always calls _refreshRepositoryMenuItems. That method clears _repositoryMenuItems and appends entries for every visible session. MenuRegistry.appendMenuItem/disposal fires a structural menu event (actions.ts:509-520); MenuWorkbenchToolBar handles it with _updateToolbar/setActions (toolbar.ts:374-405), whose ActionBar.clear path disposes all view items and removes their DOM. BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider.setSessionConfigValue emits once immediately before async resolution (baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts:4060) and _refreshNewSessionConfig emits again on completion (3772/3799).
Findings.Recommendation: Use the event's sessionId and retain a signature of each visible session's renderable property keys/order/titles. Skip MenuRegistry mutation for value-only config pulses, and replace registrations only when that schema signature or visible-session membership actually changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select a branch, worktree/isolation mode, or other repository config value in a new-session composer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The picker queues the selection per session, may complete an existing checkout operation, then calls provider.setSessionConfigValue. The provider emits an optimistic config-change pulse synchronously and later emits after asynchronous resolution. The newly added global listener performs its full visible-session/menu refresh in the synchronous event dispatch; the resulting toolbar DOM rebuild is scheduled from the structural menu event and competes with the interaction/rendering path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke repository checkout changeset operation when changing a branch that requires checkout
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one initial checkout operation per serialized branch selection, with one additional operation only after an explicit stash/commit retry choice.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same picker selection path invoked this operation before the PR; the PR only moves sequencing ownership to a shared per-session sequencer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before the selected branch value is committed when checkout is required.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch SessionConfigChanged and asynchronously resolve authoritative session config through the agent-host connection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatch/resolve sequence per committed selection; serialized for draft repository selections by session key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These provider operations and their optimistic/completion events already existed; previously the events did not structurally rebuild the repository menu and every toolbar.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resolution determines the authoritative post-selection config. The added synchronous menu-registry work runs before/as its change events are delivered but does not add an external call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: V visible session composers and P renderable schema properties. MenuRegistry events are microtask-coalesced within one refresh, so the effective cost is one structural rebuild per config pulse across V toolbars, recreating P controls per affected toolbar, rather than one rebuild per appended item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Repository selections are serialized per session by the shared SequencerByKey, but different sessions are independently keyed. Menu refresh itself is synchronous and global; each live menu toolbar responds to the coalesced structural event without a shared limiter beyond menu-event debounce/coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: provider.getSessionConfig and getCreateSessionConfig are in-memory cached reads. Dynamic completion caching remains per picker and is used only when a picker opens. The new menu refresh does not compare a cached schema signature, so warm value-only updates still clear/re-register structurally identical actions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the provider emits value-change events, the added listener unconditionally clears/re-appends menu entries, MenuRegistry emits a structural event, and MenuWorkbenchToolBar.setActions disposes/recreates action view items and DOM.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most sessions expose only a few repository properties and many users keep one visible session, so exact jank varies. Multiple pinned/visible sessions and provider-defined schemas amplify the proven recreation cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium repeated-rendering regression: value-only config changes now rebuild all repository toolbars even when action structure is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, close, pin, restore, or rearrange visible session composers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A visibleSessions publication synchronously triggers the new contribution autorun, which scans every visible session and rebuilds global repository-menu registrations. The session grid update is also reacting to the same publication, so this extra CPU/allocation runs during session-view presentation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The scan and menu-item allocation grow with V visible sessions times P renderable properties; the resulting structural event rebuilds each live repository toolbar once after coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The autorun executes synchronously with observable publication. Menu updates are coalesced/debounced, but there is no cancellation or incremental update; every publication clears and reconstructs the complete set.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session config reads are warm in-memory provider cache reads. Command/action-view factory registrations are retained by property key for contribution lifetime; menu-item registrations are fully discarded and recreated on every publication.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the O(V×P) refresh and structural toolbar update; user-visible duration depends on grid size and property count.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Visible session grids are ordinarily small, but pinned/multi-column workflows can keep several composers alive. No external boundary dominates this path; the concern is avoidable synchronous scan/allocation and subsequent DOM reconstruction.
Scenarios.Verdict: The same reported mechanism applies. A schema-signature/membership diff can preserve the required dynamic menu while avoiding complete recreation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cross the phone-layout breakpoint and render the consolidated repository/status toolbar
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The phone context-key event synchronously refreshes repository menu ordering, then each picker also re-renders to switch isolation presentation; CSS layout updates follow. No filesystem, database, network, subprocess, or IPC operation is reached by the changed layout/container code.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One refresh per breakpoint transition, scaling with visible sessions and renderable properties; transitions are infrequent compared with config pulses.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous context-key listeners followed by coalesced menu update; no async fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: All config reads are from existing in-memory state; mobile dynamic completion data remains lazy and is not fetched merely by crossing the breakpoint.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that work occurs, but low concern due to infrequency and the need to reorder controls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Breakpoint transitions are uncommon, and typical property counts are low.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: rebuilding on an actual layout/order change is intentional and bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all nine changed files and traced picker rendering, menu registry propagation, visible-session ownership, provider config events, sequencing, and transitive checkout/agent-host boundaries. Submitted one medium-confidence-impact/high-mechanism-confidence finding for global toolbar reconstruction on value-only config events; no performance regression fix was identified.
